headline: Panthers become 1st NHL team to author natural hat tricks in 3 straight games
take:
Per ESPN, Carter Verhaeghe and Sam Bennett each scored three goals as the Panthers beat the Kraken 8-3 on Saturday, making Florida the first NHL team with natural hat tricks in three straight games.

The numbers say Verhaeghe's night is mostly finishing luck, while Bennett's is the more repeatable signal. Verhaeghe has six goals on 3.04 expected goals so far this season, a gap of +2.96, and Florida does slightly better in the expected-goals share without him (-1.51 points with him on the ice). Bennett sits at three goals against 3.13 expected, essentially on par, and the Panthers' share of expected goals rises 10.97 points with him out there, with a 62.29% five-on-five share. That makes him the one driving play. Florida's 53.5% overall share and 56% at five-on-five are solid but not dominant, and the team is at -1.5 goals against expected, so the 8-3 score likely overstates them. Seattle is the opposite: a 45.6% share with +7.1 goals above expected suggests the Kraken's 5-3-1 start is running hot.
